text:
If you’re hoping for a sunset, tonight looks like a washout: light rain is already hanging on, with steadier showers and an isolated rumble of thunder developing after 8. It’ll stay mild and muggy, near 67, but south winds will gust close to 30 mph. On the lake, a Wind Advisory is up, with 2 to 4 foot waves, so this is not an evening to linger on the water. Rain should ease toward daybreak, with roughly a quarter to half an inch possible overnight.

Tomorrow is the reset, mostly sunny with a high near 78 and a west wind gusting into the 20s. The forecasters favor a dry, brighter day, though the model spread is unusually wide on shower chances, so I’d keep a light rain layer handy rather than treat the sunshine as a lock. Plan on a damp, blustery night and a much better outdoor window Thursday, especially after the morning showers fade.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Low 65°. Rain turns showery and heavier this evening as a strong warm front pushes across Vermont and northern New York. High atmospheric moisture levels will support heavy downpours and an isolated rumble of thunder (90% chance). Rainfall totals through early Thursday morning will range from 0.50 to 1.15 inches along the northern and western slopes of the Green Mountains and Adirondacks, with lower totals of 0.20 to 0.60 inches in the Champlain and Connecticut River valleys due to mountain rain shadows. A strong low-level breeze overhead will drive southwesterly wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph, especially in south-to-north oriented valleys and across Lake Champlain, where a Lake Wind Advisory remains in effect. Staying mild and humid overnight with lows in the mid-60s.
